summary: The article describes a revival of heritage grains and legumes in regional cooking, a movement that has gained speed since September 2023 and is in full swing by March 2024. It covers how chefs, farmers, an agricultural expert, and a dietitian tie the trend to flavor, sustainability, biodiversity, and social media appeal. It closes by pointing to growing CSA programs and farm shares as signs the movement will continue.
one_line: Heritage grains and legumes are returning to regional kitchens, championed by chefs and farmers for flavor, sustainability, and social media appeal.
key_facts: The revival of heritage grains and legumes in regional cooking has picked up considerable speed since September 2023, and the article is set in March 2024.
Chef Lila Thompson rolled out a new menu of dishes inspired by a simpler and more sustainable era, and sees heritage grains as a culinary canvas.
Einkorn is an ancient wheat noted for lower gluten content and superior nutrition, appealing to the gluten-sensitive.
The black turtle bean is a legume with roots in South American cuisine and is described as bursting with antioxidants.
Ezra Jacobs is a fourth-generation farmer from New Harmony, Indiana, who restored his family plot with ancient crops and belongs to a network of sustainable agriculturalists.
Dr. Anita Desai says heritage crops support biodiversity, soil health, and water conservation, and they typically need less water and fewer pesticides than modern counterparts.
Hector Ramirez, owner and head chef of Thyme and Tendril, puts a QR code on his menu so patrons can learn about the farm that grew their meal.
Jenna Clark's pop-up events, featuring dishes like 'Red Fife Wheat Berry Risotto,' have been making waves since late 2023.
Sarah Hampton plants heritage grain varieties at Willow Creek Farms on the outskirts of Asheville, North Carolina, and says it is about planting 'the right seed in the right soil at the right time.'
Heritage crops mature slowly, unlike commercial crops, which the article credits with delivering exceptional taste and nutrition.
Dishes mentioned include Blue Corn Posole and a Hoppin' John made with Sea Island Red Peas.
Hashtags such as #HeirloomBeans, #AncientGrains, and #FarmToTable are described as representing a lifestyle shift toward mindful eating.
The article notes an uptick in community-supported agriculture (CSA) programs, farm shares, and specialty food stores dedicated to heritage crops.
Dietitian Marcus Levine says cooking with these grains and legumes connects us to our past and paves the way for a healthier future.
